database.hosted: Lives inside {host}. Its version and settings are the instance's.
database.provisionFirst: Provision it first; there is nothing running to manage yet.

versions.refreshMembers: Every member restarts on the newest release of the version it runs, at the same time. Their data stays where it is.
versions.refreshInstance: The instance restarts on the newest release of the version it runs. Its data stays where it is.
versions.replicaSet: Each member restarts on {engine} {version} in turn, secondaries first, while the set keeps a primary. Then its feature compatibility version is raised, and from there it cannot go back to {current}. If a member does not come back before that, every member returns to {current}.
versions.store: The store restarts on {version} with the data it has. If it does not start, it goes back to {current}.
versions.dumpRestore: Its data is copied out, {engine} {version} starts on a new volume, and the copy is loaded into it. It is unavailable while that runs. If any step fails it goes back to {current} on its old data, which is kept either way.
versions.failed: The last upgrade did not go through: {error}
versions.onlyNewer: Only newer versions are offered: a copy from a newer version may not load into an older one.
versions.previousHint: Its data is on the volume {volume}, as it was before the upgrade. Remove that volume from the server's Storage tab once you no longer need it.
versions.revertBody: The instance restarts on {version} with the data it had before the upgrade. Anything written since stays on the newer volume and is not carried back.

topology.replicaSet: Backups are read from a secondary. A version change moves one member at a time while the set keeps a primary, then raises the feature compatibility version, after which the earlier version cannot be returned to.
topology.sharded: Copies of a sharded cluster are not offered yet. A consistent one needs the balancer stopped and every shard and the config servers copied together, and a copy taken through the router while data moves between shards can miss documents or repeat them. Version changes are not offered for a sharded cluster yet: its config servers, shards and router have to move in a set order with the balancer stopped.
topology.replicas: Backups and copies go through the primary. A version change starts the replicas again, empty, beside the new primary, and they follow it from the start.

limits.title: Resources
limits.hint: Past its memory the database is stopped and started again; past its CPU it is slowed. Blank = no limit.
limits.confirmBody: The database is started again with them. Connections drop for the few seconds that takes.

redis.clusterHint: {masters} masters, each with one replica, on this server. Clients connect in cluster mode; publish and subscribe, and streams, work as they do on one instance.
redis.clusterBackup: A backup copies every master's data file into one archive. A cluster is not restored or upgraded in place, and a backup of part of one is refused.
redis.title: How Redis keeps its data

notes.default: Redis' own snapshot schedule. What this instance was created with.
notes.cache: Nothing is written to disk. Least recently used keys are evicted to stay under the memory limit.
notes.persistent: Every write is logged and synced to disk each second, as well as snapshotted.

redis.pubsub: Publish and subscribe work in every mode.
redis.everyNode: Every node of the cluster is switched in turn.

switchBody.persistent: Redis writes everything it holds to its log first, then restarts with the log on.
switchBody.cache: Redis saves a snapshot, then restarts without writing to disk. Keys are evicted when it reaches the limit.
switchBody.default: Redis saves a snapshot, then restarts on its own snapshot schedule.

mongo.title: Replica set
mongo.hint: A single-member replica set, rs0. Change streams and multi-document transactions need one. Connection strings gain replicaSet=rs0.
mongo.offTitle: Stop running as a replica set?
mongo.onBody: The instance restarts with a replica set of one member. If it does not start that way, it is put back.
mongo.offBody: The instance restarts as a standalone server with the same data. Change streams and transactions stop working.

pitr.title: Continuous archiving
pitr.hint: Every change is archived, with a base backup each day, so the instance can be rebuilt as it was at any moment in the window. The archive is on this server's disk: it covers mistakes, not a lost disk.
pitr.onBody: The instance restarts with archiving on, and takes its first base backup.
pitr.offBody: The instance restarts without archiving and the archive is deleted. Nothing before now can be recovered afterwards.
pitr.window: Recoverable from {from} until about a minute ago. {count, plural, one {# base backup} other {# base backups}} kept.
pitr.firstBackup: Taking the first base backup. Nothing can be recovered until it finishes.
pitr.recoverHint: The recovery lands in a new database beside this one, with the same accounts. This one is not touched.
pitr.outsideWindow: Pick a moment inside the window above.
pitr.confirmBody: A new database, {name}, is created from the base backup before that moment and replays the log up to it. That can take a while on a busy instance.

copy.sourcesUnreadable: Could not list the databases to copy from
copy.needsPermission: Copying data in needs permission to manage databases.
copy.hint: Replaces everything in {name} with a copy of another database. A backup of {name} is taken first when it is protected.
copy.noOther: No other {engine} database in this project is running.
copy.useScheme: Use a {scheme}:// address with a host name and the database at the end.
copy.readInside: Read from inside this database's container, so the host has to be reachable from its server.
copy.confirmBody: Everything in {name} is replaced with a copy of {source}. Follow it under Activity.

database.nothingRun: Nothing has been run on this database yet.

buckets.endpointHint: Reachable by name from the services in this environment. Its keys are in Connection details and in references such as S3_ENDPOINT.
buckets.unmanaged: Also in the store, made outside Polaris: {names}.
buckets.removeDescription: Every object in it and every key for it goes. This cannot be undone.
buckets.revokeBody: Anything using this key loses access to the bucket at once.
buckets.copySecret: Copy the secret now. It is not shown again.
buckets.expiryHint: Objects written under a prefix from now on are deleted at that age.
buckets.presignHint: Lets whoever holds it download or upload one object until it expires, without a key.
buckets.baseUrlPlaceholder: Address it is used on, if not inside the environment (https://files.example.com)
buckets.replicationHint: Every change is copied, one way, into a bucket of another store on the same server.
buckets.candidatesUnreadable: Could not list the buckets to replicate into
buckets.noCandidates: No bucket in another store on this server. Create a second object store here first.

metrics.reading: Reading the volume from inside the service
metrics.noDu: The image has no du, so its size cannot be read.
metrics.gaps: Usage is measured from inside the service that mounts the volume, so a stopped service leaves gaps.

files.unattachedBody: This volume is not attached to a service, and its data is only reachable from inside the container that mounts it.
files.stoppedBody: Files are read from inside {service}. Deploy it to browse {path}.
files.readInsideService: Read from inside the service at {path}.

settings.unattached: This volume is not attached to a service.
settings.mountHint: Where this volume comes from and where the service sees it. Changes apply the next time the service is recreated.
settings.regionHint: Volumes live on the same server as the service that mounts them.
settings.wipeHint: Destroys everything inside it and keeps the volume itself.
settings.wipeNeedsRunning: The service has to be running to reach the data
settings.deleteHint: Detaches the mount from the service. The next deploy starts without it.
settings.wipeDescription: Everything in this volume is destroyed. The volume itself stays, so the service keeps its mount.
settings.deleteDescription: The mount is detached from the service. Whether the data goes with it is up to you.
settings.destroyDataHint: Off by default. Detaching a volume and destroying what is in it are two different intentions, and only one of them can be taken back.

help.volume: A named volume managed by Docker. Good for opaque data like a database's files.
help.bind: A folder on this service's server. Persists across redeploys and is browsable in the Files tab.
help.nas: A folder on a host-mounted storage connection - it lives on the NAS and can be managed as a Drive folder.

volumeForm.pickService: Pick a service for this volume
volumeForm.name: Name
volumeForm.noConnections: No NAS connections found. Add an NFS, SMB, or UniFi UNAS connection in Drive first.
volumeForm.autoPath: Polaris creates and organizes it under {path}.
volumeForm.subpathHint: A subpath (no leading slash, no `..`). Created if it does not exist.
volumeForm.noServices: Add a service first - a volume mounts into a service's container.

topology.readReplicasHint: They follow the primary by GTID replication and refuse writes. The connection details gain a URI for reading from them.
topology.replicaSetHint: {count} members on this server, finding each other by name. Connection strings list them all.
topology.shardedHint: A config server set of {setSize}, {shards} shards of {setSize} members and a router: {containers} containers. Each collection stays on one shard until your application shards it with a shard key (shardCollection). Backups and version changes are not offered for it yet.

workspace.needsManage: Browsing this database needs the right to manage Deploy and the project's databases.

data.readOnly: Read-only. Browse and query without changing anything.
data.writable: Changes allowed. Edits, new rows and statements write to the live database.
data.allowBody: Edits, new rows, deleted rows and statements will write to this database straight away. Read-only comes back the next time this panel opens.

stats.unreadable: The database did not answer. Check that it is running.
stats.enableHint: PostgreSQL records which statements run, and how long they take, once pg_stat_statements is loaded.
stats.enableBody: The database restarts with pg_stat_statements loaded, which takes a few seconds and drops open connections. If it does not come back, it is put back as it was.
stats.queriesUnavailable: This server does not record statement statistics.
stats.freezeRisk: Transaction IDs are {age} old, past the {limit} at which PostgreSQL forces a freeze. Vacuum the oldest tables below.
stats.xidAge: Oldest transaction ID: {age} of {limit} before a forced freeze.
stats.bloat: {count, plural, one {# table has} other {# tables have}} more than {percent}% dead rows.
stats.vacuumBody: Runs VACUUM (ANALYZE) on the table. Reads and writes carry on while it runs.
stats.noUnused: Every index has been used since statistics were last reset.
stats.unusedHint: Never scanned since statistics were last reset. Candidates for removal, if that covers a normal week.

config.regenerateHint: Services that read this database's variables restart with the new password.
config.regenerateBody: Open connections that use the old password stop working.
config.noDependents: No running service reads this database's variables.
config.dependents: {count, plural, one {This service restarts: {names}.} other {These # services restart: {names}.}}
config.regeneratedRestarting: {count, plural, one {Password changed. Restarting {names}.} other {Password changed. Restarting # services: {names}.}}
config.extensionsHosted: Installed into this database only, with its own account.
config.extensionsUnreadable: The list of extensions could not be read.
config.installBody: Runs CREATE EXTENSION in this database.
config.installPreload: pg_stat_statements has to be loaded when the server starts, so the database restarts first. It is put back as it was if it does not come back.
config.uninstallBody: Runs DROP EXTENSION without CASCADE: if anything depends on it, PostgreSQL refuses and nothing changes.

connect.unreadable: The connection details could not be read.
connect.privateIntro: Services in this environment reach the database by name. Add a variable to the service and give it this reference; Polaris fills it in on every deploy.
connect.referenceHint: For example DATABASE_URL = the reference above. A copy of the environment points at its own {name}.
connect.variablesHint: Each one is a reference you can give a service's variable. Click to copy.
connect.publicWarning: Anyone who can reach this port can try to sign in. Keep the password private, and close the port when it is not needed.
connect.closeBody: The database is deployed again without the port. Clients outside the server lose access.
connect.publishBody: The database is deployed again with the port open on its server, which takes a few seconds and drops open connections.
connect.notPublic: Only services on this server can reach it. Publish it on a port to reach it from your machine.
connect.noAddress: Published on port {port}, but Polaris does not know this server's address. Set it under Domains.
connect.hostedPrivate: This database lives inside another instance. Publish that instance to reach it from outside.
